input.body:
## Bug

Desktop update feedback is misleading in two related situations:

1. A manual **Check for updates** can remain in its loading state after the main process has already published a terminal result. Navigating away and returning remounts the view and reveals the completed result.
2. Automatic checks and downloads produce no sidebar feedback until the update is fully downloaded, making a working automatic update look inactive and leaving users unsure whether they must update manually.

**Source:** Local Codex report with screenshots and a follow-up report from Prateek; no public chat URL  
**Observed:** macOS, AO `0.12.7-nightly.202608221348`  
**Analyzed against:** `858146266`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** Medium — update behavior is degraded, with manual checking as a workaround.

## Reproduction

### Stuck manual loading

1. Open Settings → Updates.
2. Click **Check for updates**.
3. Let the updater publish a matching terminal status such as `not-available` while the IPC invocation remains unsettled.
4. The button and status panel remain in the checking state.
5. Navigate away and return; the completed status appears.

### Missing automatic progress

1. Seed or receive updater status `{ state: "available" }` or `{ state: "downloading" }`.
2. Observe the sidebar footer.
3. No update information is rendered until status becomes `downloaded`, at which point the existing **Restart to update** button appears.

## Root Cause

- `UpdatesSection` owns a renderer-local pending flag whose lifetime is coupled to the IPC promise rather than the updater status event. Electron can publish the terminal event before the invocation settles, so completed state is masked by stale local loading state.
- `Sidebar` explicitly renders its update row only for `status.state === "downloaded"`; `available` and `downloading` return `null`.

## Fix

- Correlate manual update checks with request IDs and clear local pending state when a matching non-checking status arrives, even if the IPC promise remains pending.
- Show informational, non-clickable sidebar states for available updates and download progress; preserve the existing restart/install button only for a staged download.

## Verification

- `cd frontend && npm test -- --run src/renderer/components/Sidebar.test.tsx src/renderer/components/GlobalSettingsForm.test.tsx src/main/auto-updater.test.ts`
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck`

## Related

- [#2377](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2377) — original downloaded-only restart-row specification.
- [PR #4144](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4144) — update feedback redesign that introduced the renderer-local pending state.
- [#3526](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3526) — automatic updater failures can remain silent; recovery visibility is related but outside this fix.

input.body:
## Bug

Editing an earlier human message in a Codex Chat session consistently fails with `CHAT_RESUME_FAILED` instead of creating and activating the edited conversation branch.

**Source:** Reported in AO Chat with an attached screenshot  
**Analyzed against:** `9c1797cde982c0cdf925c74ea4588cf5f3fbcb57`  
**AO daemon:** checkout build (`dev`) on `127.0.0.1:3001`  
**Codex CLI:** `0.148.0`  
**OS:** macOS arm64  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P1 — the prompt-edit workflow is broken whenever the edited prompt has a preceding provider turn.

![Reported `CHAT_RESUME_FAILED` error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-codex-edit-active-writer/.issue-assets/codex-edit-active-writer/reported-error.png)

## Reproduction

1. Start a Codex session in Chat mode.
2. Complete at least two human/assistant turns.
3. Edit the second human message and submit it.
4. Observe `the stored provider conversation could not be resumed (CHAT_RESUME_FAILED)`.

A minimized live provider harness reproduces the backend boundary directly:

1. Start a real Codex app-server conversation.
2. Complete one turn.
3. Call `thread/fork` through that turn.
4. While the source app-server remains open, start a second app-server and call `thread/resume` for the fork id.

This failed three out of three times with app-server error `-32600: thread <id> already has an active writer`. Waiting two seconds did not change the result. Closing the source connection before resume made the same harness pass twice.

## Root Cause

`Service.EditMessage` calls `ChatForker.Fork`, receives the new provider conversation id, and immediately calls `driver.Resume` for that id on a new app-server process. Codex `thread/fork` already loads the new thread and emits `thread/started`, so the source app-server owns the fork as its active writer. The second process cannot resume it.

AO only closes the source controller after the replacement controller has been created and installed. That point is unreachable because replacement resume fails first.

The existing service fake models `Fork` as returning a passive string and therefore cannot express provider writer ownership. Adapter tests cover fork and resume independently rather than chaining them as the edit flow does.

## Fix

Preserve AO's one-writer and failure-recovery guarantees while changing the edit handoff sequence so a fork is not resumed by a second process while its creating app-server still owns it. Add regression coverage with a writer-aware fake plus an opt-in live Codex fork/resume test.

## Impact

- Editing the first prompt is unaffected because it starts a fresh provider conversation.
- Editing any later prompt is broken for Codex Chat sessions.
- The original conversation and worktree remain intact; the edit is refused rather than silently losing history.

## Related

- [PR #3676](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3676) — introduced Codex prompt editing with conversation branches.
input.title: Codex prompt edit fails because forked thread already has an active writer

## Bug

On macOS, invoking the native **View → Toggle Developer Tools** command (or its `Cmd+Option+I` accelerator) can throw an uncaught exception in Electron's main process instead of opening DevTools.

The reporter sees the standard “A JavaScript error occurred in the main process” dialog with:

```text
Uncaught Exception:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toggleDevTools')
    at webContentsMethod (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:31239)
    at Object.execute (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:28651)
    at MenuItem.click (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:35249)
    at a._executeCommand (node:electron/js2c/browser_init:2:40710)
```

![macOS main-process error after toggling DevTools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-macos-toggle-devtools-crash-20260823/.issue-assets/macos-toggle-devtools-crash-20260823/devtools-crash.png)

**Source:** Direct Codex report on 2026-08-23 (no public chat URL)  
**Reported by:** @illegalcall  
**First observed:** 2026-08-23 on a nightly build; exact regression onset is not established  
**Analyzed against:** `c86b58d04a38ce669be3215ab0834e29cf2c0d30` (`origin/main`)  
**AO desktop version:** `0.12.7-nightly.202608181938` (bundled daemon reports `dev`, healthy on port `3001`)  
**Environment:** macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple Silicon (`arm64`)  
**Priority:** P2 — the action crashes the Electron main process, but the scope is bounded to the native DevTools command and an in-app DevTools path is available  
**Confidence:** High — the stack, platform menu setup, and exact failing mechanism have been traced; an existing tested PR implements the same fix

## Reproduction

1. Launch Agent Orchestrator on macOS.
2. Focus a surface backed by a `WebContentsView` (the Browser panel is the common case).
3. Choose **View → Toggle Developer Tools** from the native macOS application menu, or press `Cmd+Option+I`.
4. Observe the uncaught `toggleDevTools` exception and main-process error dialog.

## Expected

DevTools opens for the focused AO surface, or the shell surface as a safe fallback, without terminating the main process.

## Actual

Electron's native menu command attempts to call `toggleDevTools` through an undefined focused-window target and throws an uncaught exception in the main process.

## Root Cause

`frontend/src/main.ts` installs AO's guarded application menu only on Windows. On macOS, Electron's default application menu remains active, including the built-in `role: "toggleDevTools"` command.

AO composes its window from a `BaseWindow` and `WebContentsView` surfaces. When focus belongs to a `WebContentsView`, Electron's built-in role resolves no focused `BrowserWindow`, then its internal `webContentsMethod` path attempts to access `toggleDevTools` on an undefined target. This matches the `MenuItem.click` stack in the report.

AO's custom titlebar IPC handler and Windows menu already route DevTools through guarded AO logic; the native default macOS menu is the unguarded path.

## Suggested Fix

Install an explicit macOS application menu and replace only the built-in DevTools role with a click handler that:

1. toggles DevTools for the last-focused AO browser surface; and
2. falls back to the shell `webContents` when no browser surface is available.

Keep the standard macOS app roles (About, Services, Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Quit) when replacing Electron's default menu.

## Impact

- A standard macOS menu item and accelerator can crash the Electron main process.
- No data loss was observed in this report.
- Workaround: avoid the native menu/accelerator and use AO's in-app DevTools control where available.

## Related

- [PR #3910](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3910) — open, tested implementation of the traced fix; awaiting review and currently has no closing issue reference.

input.author: Pulkit7070
input.body:
## Summary
The renderer opens Server-Sent-Events streams — `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/workspace/events` and `/api/v1/notifications/stream` — with `EventSource`, which reconnects **immediately on any failed connection, with no backoff**. If the daemon returns a transient 5xx while *setting up* the stream, the client reconnects in a tight loop, turning one brief failure into a sustained burst of failed requests and high CPU on both sides.

## Where it happens
- Handler: `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/sessions.go` → `streamWorkspaceChanges` (and the notifications stream controller). These can only return 5xx during setup, before `w.WriteHeader(200)`.
- Setup failure points: `WorkspaceWatchPaths` → `sessionWorkspaceRecord` (its `GetSession` branch wraps the error untyped as `fmt.Errorf("get %s: %w", …)` → 500), and `workspacewatch.Watch` / `watchRoot`.
- Renderer: the `EventSource` consumer for these streams reconnects with no backoff.

## Reproduction
The daemon port is in `~/.ao/running.json`.
1. Healthy stream (baseline): `curl -N http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v1/sessions/<id>/workspace/events` → `200`, stream stays open. ✅ verified
2. Missing workspace: same call for a session whose workspace dir is gone → `404 SESSION_WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND` (already typed on current `main`). ✅ verified — so the common missing-path case is *not* the culprit.
3. Trigger the amplification: put the daemon under DB-lock contention (see #3963) so `GetSession` intermittently errors → stream setup returns `500` → watch the renderer immediately reconnect and re-fail in a loop (visible in the access log and as CPU spikes). A single stuck stream produces a large, self-sustaining burst.

## Suggested fix
- Renderer: exponential backoff + jitter on SSE reconnect; stop reconnecting when the session is terminated and on any `4xx`.
- Daemon (optional): send `Retry-After` on transient setup failures so clients pace reconnects.

## Related
- #3963 (DB lock contention → the transient 5xx this amplifies)
- #1321 (RFC: remove polling → reactive sync)
input.title: bug(daemon+renderer): SSE streams reconnect with no backoff, amplifying a transient setup 5xx into a request storm

input.author: Pulkit7070
input.body:
## Summary
Handlers and services return raw `fmt.Errorf(...)` for conditions that are **transient or expected**, and `backend/internal/httpd/envelope.go` maps any non-`apierr` error to `INTERNAL_ERROR` / `500`. As a result, transient DB contention (#3963), client-state conditions, and genuine faults all surface as **identical opaque 500s** — the reliability signal is polluted by non-faults, and the real cause is only visible in the daemon log, never in the API response.

## Where
- `backend/internal/httpd/envelope.go` — the `INTERNAL_ERROR` fallback for untyped errors.
- Example offender: `backend/internal/service/session/workspace_files.go` → `sessionWorkspaceRecord` wraps `GetSession` as `fmt.Errorf("get %s: %w", …)` (untyped → 500).

## Reproduction
1. `rg "envelope.WriteError" backend/internal/httpd/controllers` and follow each to the service call it forwards — the ones returning plain `fmt.Errorf` (not `apierr.*`) become opaque 500s.
2. Drive any such handler while the DB is under contention (#3963): the response is a `500` with code `INTERNAL_ERROR` and no specific `error_code`, indistinguishable from a real server fault.

## Suggested fix
- Map transient/contention DB errors to a typed `503` (retryable) with a stable code, and expected states to typed `4xx`, so the 5xx surface reflects only real server faults.
- Land Sentry error capture (PRs #4180 desktop / #4181 mobile) so the remaining genuine 500s carry a grouped stack and root cause.

## Related
- #3963, #3649, #2699, #3408 (instances of the opacity); #4180 / #4181 (visibility)

input.author: niwant-tada
input.body:
## Bug

A Phoenix project configured with worker agent `cursor` and model `composer-2.5-fast` exposed two related spawn failures:

1. A normal prompted spawn failed with `chat mode unsupported for harness: cursor has no chat driver (SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED)` and created no session.
2. Explicit `--mode tui` created `phoenix-10`, but Cursor exited before accepting a follow-up. A disposable reproduction showed the underlying startup race: Cursor stops at its interactive MCP approval screen, while `ao send` returns success and the follow-up is consumed by that screen instead of reaching the agent.

**Source:** AO conversation, session `phoenix-1`, 2026-08-23  
**Reported by:** current AO user  
**Analyzed against:** `6cba6344c7081f2984927ca5f15140f99115c5c0` (`origin/main`)  
**AO CLI version:** `dev`  
**Desktop build:** `0.12.7-nightly.202608231948`  
**Priority:** medium / P2 — spawn is degraded, but manual TUI recovery exists  
**Confidence:** High for the reproduced startup-input loss; Medium for the exact `phoenix-10` exit because the Cursor process had already exited and produced no worker log

## Environment

- macOS Darwin 25.6.0 arm64
- zsh
- bundled binary only: `/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao`
- healthy daemon on `127.0.0.1:3001`
- Cursor Agent `2026.08.11-e8db854`, authenticated
- Cursor model `composer-2.5-fast`
- tmux 3.7c
- no Go binary in `PATH`

## Reproduction

### Original omitted-mode failure

```sh
AO_BIN="/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/daemon/ao"
"$AO_BIN" status --json # port 3001
"$AO_BIN" spawn \
  --project phoenix \
  --name cursor-chat-repro \
  --prompt "Reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_REPRO_OK and wait for follow-up."
```

Observed:

```text
spawn: chat mode unsupported for harness: cursor has no chat driver (SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED)
```

Exit status was 1 and no session row was created.

### Reproduced TUI startup-input loss

```sh
"$AO_BIN" spawn \
  --project phoenix \
  --name cursor-tui-repro \
  --mode tui \
  --prompt "Reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_TUI_REPRO_OK and wait for follow-up."
```

1. Cursor displays `MCP Server Approval Required` for the project MCP server before it consumes the prompt.
2. While that screen is visible, run:

```sh
"$AO_BIN" send \
  --session phoenix-13 \
  --message "Follow-up: reply with exactly AO_CURSOR_CHAT_FOLLOWUP_OK."
```

3. `ao send` exits 0, but the message is not shown or processed by Cursor.
4. After the MCP gate clears, a second `ao send` is delivered and Cursor replies normally.

For `phoenix-10`, durable state changed from idle to exited about three seconds after spawn. Its tmux shell remained alive, `cursor-agent` was gone, no Cursor native session id was recorded, and no Cursor `worker.log` was created.

## Root Cause

The CLI correctly omits `mode` when `--mode` is not passed (`backend/internal/cli/spawn.go`). The originally running packaged daemon resolved the saved Chat default but had no Cursor Chat driver, producing `SESSION_MODE_UNSUPPORTED`.

Current `origin/main` already contains both protections:

- inherited Chat preflight failures fall back to TUI in `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:771`
- Cursor is registered through `cursor-agent acp` in `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/registry/registry.go:62`

After the daemon restarted, the same omitted-mode reproduction no longer errored and created a TUI session, confirming the original Chat failure was tied to the running packaged build rather than current source.

The remaining TUI race is in current source:

- Cursor TUI launches as `cursor-agent --model composer-2.5-fast -- <prompt>` and does not bypass MCP approval (`backend/pkg/agentruntime/command.go:386`).
- AO Cursor hooks begin at `sessionStart` and tool/prompt events (`backend/internal/adapters/agent/cursor/hooks.go:57`), so the pre-session MCP dialog emits no blocked activity signal.
- The session therefore remains durably idle. `sessionguard.Deliver` refuses only known blocked decisions, so it permits the write (`backend/internal/sessionguard/guard.go:142`).
- tmux pastes the text and always presses Enter (`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:575`). Cursor consumes that input at the approval screen.
- `ao send` has no provider acknowledgement for Cursor and returns success once tmux accepts the keystrokes (`backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:2887`).

## Suggested Fix

- Add a provider-neutral startup-ready gate for TUI sessions, satisfied by the first native session-start/prompt-ready signal.
- Queue or reject follow-ups with a typed not-ready error until that gate is satisfied.
- Do not auto-approve MCP servers under the default permission policy.
- Add a Cursor regression test where a pre-session dialog is present and verify that no follow-up is reported delivered until Cursor is ready.

## Workaround

- Install/restart into a build containing the merged Cursor ACP driver, then use Chat mode.
- On older builds, use `--mode tui`, answer the Cursor MCP approval screen manually, and resend the follow-up only after the Cursor prompt is visible.

## Verification and PR status

No fix PR was attempted. The machine has no Go toolchain, and repository policy requires `go build ./...` plus `go test ./...` before pushing a backend fix. No system software was installed and no unverified patch was pushed.

Dependency check: Cursor Agent `2026.08.11-e8db854` exposes the hidden `cursor-agent acp` command and matches the minimum version used by the merged Cursor Chat driver. The repository uses `github.com/coder/acp-go-sdk v0.13.5`, which is also the latest published SDK release.

## Related

- [#3712](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3712) — earlier unsupported-Chat Cursor spawn report in the desktop composer
- [PR #3715](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3715) — frontend routing of unsupported Chat agents to TUI
- [PR #4233](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4233) — inherited Chat default falls back to TUI
- [PR #4201](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4201) — merged Cursor ACP Chat driver tested against Cursor `2026.08.11-e8db854`
- [#3634](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3634) — related `ao send` success-versus-delivery semantics

input.author: whoisasx
input.body:
## Bug

After an AO worker switches from Claude/`claude-code` to Codex, Codex can process billable turns while **Cost & Usage continues to show only Claude**. The failure is deterministic when the first Codex rollout `session_meta` JSONL record exceeds the usage collector's 65,536-byte discovery limit.

**Source:** live local AO production audit on 2026-08-24  
**Reported by:** AO user report for `reverb-29` / `4218-subscription`  
**Production build:** `d4ae9b318e2a14748661c5b71ad589c2f1153521` (collector file byte-identical to the analyzed checkout)  
**Analyzed against:** `2fa9672c77b3c7ca8a70494d8ea38ab9a2c91906`  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced from persisted switch, native rollout, observation, ledger, API, and UI state and traced to an exact bounded-reader failure.  
**Priority:** P2 — usage accounting is omitted for affected sessions, but runtime work continues and the affected set is bounded/recoverable.

## User-visible impact

For affected sessions:

1. The harness switch completes and AO persists `harness=codex` plus the correct Codex native session ID and rollout path.
2. Codex processes later user turns and emits cumulative `token_count` observations.
3. AO leaves the Codex usage binding in `source_discovery_pending` with no `usage_sources` row.
4. No Codex model-usage ledger events are created.
5. The usage API therefore returns only the pre-switch Claude contribution, and the Summary sidebar faithfully renders Claude only.

The observations were not assigned to the old Claude harness; they never crossed the Codex source-discovery boundary.

## Reproduction

1. Start an AO worker using Claude with enough history to produce a large switch continuation.
2. Switch it to Codex.
3. Let Codex process at least one turn and emit a `token_count` rollout record.
4. Ensure Codex's first rollout `session_meta` line contains more than 65,536 bytes (a near-limit handoff naturally does this).
5. Inspect the Codex usage binding and Cost & Usage response.

Expected: the Codex rollout is registered, historical records are ingested, and both Claude and Codex appear in the session usage response.

Actual: the binding remains `source_discovery_pending`; source/event counts remain zero; the API and Summary omit Codex.

## Verified affected and control sessions

Audit scope was every persisted agent switch across all locally registered projects (`reverb`, `scratch`, and `super-30`), including active and terminated sessions. There were 14 Claude-to-Codex switch attempts across six unique sessions; six completed. No other harness-pair switches were present.

| Session | Display name | Completed switch (UTC) | First `session_meta` line | Post-switch Codex use | Codex in Cost & Usage | Classification |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| `reverb-29` | `4218-subscription` | 2026-08-23 17:52:21 | 89,596 B | 176 observations; latest cumulative 23,389,905 processed tokens | No | Affected |
| `reverb-30` | `4026-sidebar_dots` | 2026-08-24 05:38:52 | 22,177 B | 67 observations; 67 ledger events | Yes | Correct control |
| `reverb-31` | `term-select-scroll` | 2026-08-24 04:47:29 | 90,941 B | 93 observations; latest cumulative 15,927,562 | No | Affected |
| `reverb-33` | `sidebar-dnd` | 2026-08-24 04:42:21 | 91,344 B | 60 observations; latest cumulative 4,923,012 | No | Affected |
| `reverb-35` | `long-session-names` | 2026-08-24 04:46:37 | 91,546 B | 70 observations; latest cumulative 8,321,724 | No | Affected |
| `reverb-38` | `agent-system-guide` | 2026-08-23 19:50:39 | 55,410 B | 95 observations; 93 ledger events | Yes | Correct control |

The two skipped `reverb-38` observations had zero measurable token components and inconsistent `last.total_tokens`; they were correctly treated as anomalies and are unrelated to discovery.

Aggregate at the audit snapshot:

- 6 completed switches with real post-switch Codex turns.
- 4 affected, 2 correct controls.
- 561 raw Codex observations total; 399 belonged to affected sessions.
- 160 Codex ledger events total; affected sessions had zero.
- 52,562,203 cumulative processed Codex tokens were visible in affected raw observations but absent from the ledger.
- Across all 20 locally persisted Codex usage bindings, 16 had sources and these exact four remained pending. No additional active or terminated local sessions were affected.

Eight failed switch attempts are false positives if inventory code counts `target_harness=codex` without requiring a completed switch/native rollout. They did not establish comparable post-switch Codex use.

## Timeline and evidence

- The six successful switches completed between 2026-08-23 17:52 UTC and 2026-08-24 05:39 UTC.
- The daemon restarted at 2026-08-24 04:43:46 UTC. Affected switches occurred both before and after it; a correct control also occurred after it.
- Persisted session rows for all six identified Codex as the current harness and held a correct native Codex identity/rollout. `reverb-31` later resumed under a new AO launch ID while retaining the same native Codex ID and rollout; its failure persisted.
- Affected bindings were retried approximately every 30 seconds, updating their timestamps but deterministically remaining `source_discovery_pending`.
- Fresh usage API requests already omitted Codex. The result was not a stale browser cache.

The `ao send` `INTERNAL_ERROR` observed around the `reverb-29` switch is not causal. Its switch handoff timed out, but the switch completed, the persisted Codex identity is correct, seven later user follow-ups reached Codex, and 176 Codex token observations exist. This distinguishes that transient control/runtime failure from the independent usage-discovery defect.

## Root cause

`backend/internal/service/usage/collector.go` defines:

```go
maxCodexSessionMeta = 64 << 10
```

`discoverCodexPath` validates each candidate by calling `codexSessionMetaMatches`, which calls `readCodexSessionMeta`. That function uses:

```go
bufio.NewReaderSize(file, maxCodexSessionMeta+1).ReadSlice('\n')
```

When the first JSONL record is over 64 KiB, `ReadSlice` returns `bufio.ErrBufferFull`. The function returns `(false)` before unmarshalling the otherwise valid metadata, and discovery silently rejects the candidate.

The same reader participates in initial hook source attribution, startup active-session backfill, and periodic reconciliation. Every repair path therefore repeats the same deterministic rejection.

This is **before** the normal usage parser/ingestor. `backend/internal/observe/usage/ingestor.go` already permits records up to `1 << 20` (1 MiB), so the affected records are ingestible but never registered as sources.

The failed boundary is:

```text
valid Codex rollout
  -> bounded session_meta discovery (fails at 64 KiB)
  -> no usage_sources row
  -> watcher/ingestor never runs
  -> no model_usage_events or OpenAI detail rows
  -> API aggregation has no Codex rows
  -> Summary has nothing Codex to render
```

A secondary observability problem is that `source_discovery_pending` is currently treated as benign by session integrity aggregation, so these API responses reported `incomplete: false` despite missing a provider source.

## Why agent switches produce oversized first records

The switch path permits a finalized handoff continuation up to `96 << 10` bytes (`handoffContinuationMaxBytes`). It appends that continuation to the target's hidden system prompt. Codex then serializes the complete prompt into the first rollout record under `payload.base_instructions.text`.

The physical line therefore includes more than the capped handoff:

- up to 96 KiB of continuation,
- roughly 8 KiB of AO base/protocol instructions in the observed cases,
- project/agent rules,
- the JSON envelope and escaping overhead.

Observed total AO prompt sizes were 83,619–84,953 bytes for three affected controls plus 84,585 bytes for the fourth; JSON serialization expanded the physical lines to 89–91 KiB. The working controls had smaller continuations and stayed below 64 KiB.

Thus the existing limits contain an invalid invariant: a switch may legitimately generate a 96 KiB continuation while source discovery rejects the complete serialized record above 64 KiB. Project rules can also enlarge the record, so this is not inherently switch-only.

## Blast radius

Any Codex rollout whose first `session_meta` record exceeds 64 KiB can fail discovery, including:

- Claude-to-Codex switches with large continuation context,
- fresh Codex sessions with large project/agent rules,
- restored native Codex sessions,
- Codex child/subagent rollouts,
- archived/relocated rollout discovery.

The local canonical database contained no affected sessions beyond the four listed above, but the defect is product-wide and data-dependent rather than tied to those identities.

## Why tests and CI missed it

- Collector fixtures create tiny `session_meta` envelopes and omit realistic `base_instructions`.
- The existing “large rollout” test adds many records **after a small first line**, so it tests total file size rather than first-record size.
- Switch tests enforce the independent 96 KiB continuation bound using fake runtimes but never serialize a production-shaped Codex first record and pass it through usage discovery.
- Parser tests cover the 1 MiB ingestion limit independently; no cross-package test enforces `switch prompt <= discovery record <= ingestion record`.
- CI does not launch a real Codex provider, so it never observes the provider's first-record serialization shape.

## Immediate safe recovery

After deploying the reader fix, restart once to run active-session backfill or allow periodic reconciliation to run. The existing four bindings should register their rollout from byte offset zero and ingest historical records to EOF.

Do **not** truncate/copy provider rollouts, delete bindings, or manually insert usage events.

Double-counting protections already exist:

- all four affected bindings currently have zero sources/events;
- sources are unique by binding/artifact/generation;
- events are unique by binding/source event key;
- `ApplyUsageChunk` atomically validates events, inserts details, and advances cursor/baseline in one transaction;
- replaying identical events is idempotent and conflicts roll back.

If an affected session terminates before deployment, perform the same controlled targeted reconciliation against its preserved binding/source rather than manual ledger writes.

## Smallest durable fix

Raise the bounded Codex metadata-record limit from 64 KiB to **1 MiB**, matching the existing ingestion record limit. Continue reading only the first record and retain all existing provider-root, symlink, native-ID, parent-attribution, candidate-count, and cancellation checks.

A 1 MiB bound comfortably covers the permitted 96 KiB handoff plus the rest of the serialized prompt while remaining finite. Records above that limit should remain rejected; follow-up hardening can make the rejection explicit and surface persistent discovery-pending state as `incomplete: true`.

Where package boundaries allow, discovery and ingestion should derive their record ceiling from one shared contract to prevent future drift.

## Security and operational limits

- The first record may contain hidden system instructions and handoff context. Do not log or persist its text outside the provider-owned rollout; parse only identity/source fields.
- Keep a strict bounded read; do not replace it with an unbounded scanner/read-all.
- Preserve first-record-only processing, provider-root/symlink validation, native ID/parent verification, context cancellation, and the existing finite candidate search.
- Rejecting a record above 1 MiB should produce sanitized diagnostics without prompt contents.

## Regression test matrix

Focused fix coverage:

- [ ] A valid Codex `session_meta` first record above 64 KiB and below 1 MiB is matched.
- [ ] Native ID and parent thread matching still work with the large record.
- [ ] A first record above 1 MiB remains rejected without an unbounded read.
- [ ] Existing malformed JSON, wrong native ID, wrong parent, symlink/root escape, and small-record behavior remains unchanged.

Follow-up integration coverage:

- [ ] Codex session-start hook with native ID but no transcript path discovers a large-metadata rollout and clears pending state.
- [ ] Active-session backfill ingests historical token records from offset zero.
- [ ] Reconciliation is idempotent across restart/replay.
- [ ] A near-96-KiB switch continuation serialized in a production-shaped Codex envelope reaches OpenAI/model ledger rows.
- [ ] Usage API returns both pre-switch Claude and post-switch Codex contributions.
- [ ] Persistent discovery-pending state makes integrity incomplete and is surfaced by the Summary UI.

## Bug

Nightly `0.12.7-nightly.202608241447` prints `can't find terminfo database` repeatedly in every TUI agent session. New TUI attaches fail, and already-running TUI sessions begin showing the same error after updating because the updated daemon attaches with the newly bundled tmux client.

**Source:** User report in an AO session on 2026-08-24 (no public chat URL available)  
**Analyzed against:** `ea895fa8b` (regression introduced by `c9a0adb21`, PR [#4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293))  
**Observed artifact:** macOS arm64 desktop nightly `0.12.7-nightly.202608241447`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P1 — TUI attachment is a core workflow and the packaged-app launch path has no practical in-app workaround.

## Reproduction

On macOS arm64 with the affected nightly installed:

1. Locate the staged bundled binary at `~/.ao/runtime/tmux/0.12.7-nightly.202608241447-darwin-arm64/tmux`.
2. Create an isolated session:
   ```sh
   BUNDLED_TMUX="$HOME/.ao/runtime/tmux/0.12.7-nightly.202608241447-darwin-arm64/tmux"
   "$BUNDLED_TMUX" -L ao-terminfo-repro -f /dev/null new-session -d -s triage 'sleep 30'
   ```
3. Attach using the same terminal arguments/environment as `Runtime.Attach`:
   ```sh
   TERM=xterm-256color "$BUNDLED_TMUX" -L ao-terminfo-repro -u -T RGB attach-session -t triage
   ```
4. Observe two lines of `can't find terminfo database`; the client exits with status 1.

`TERMINFO=/usr/share/terminfo` makes the same attach succeed, and `/usr/bin/infocmp xterm-256color` confirms the system entry exists.

## Root Cause

`frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:136-158` builds a private static ncurses/libtinfo under a temporary CI prefix, then `frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:184-190` statically links that library into tmux. The ncurses configuration does not specify portable system terminfo directories or embedded fallback entries.

The resulting shipped binary contains this compile-time database location:

```text
/Users/runner/work/agent-orchestrator/agent-orchestrator/.cache/bundled-tmux/darwin-arm64-r3-3.5a-2.1.12-stable-6.5-2.10.0/prefix/share/terminfo
```

That directory does not exist on an installed user's machine. Only the tmux executable and licenses are copied into `frontend/tmux`; no terminfo database is packaged.

`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:722-728` launches the bundled tmux client for every terminal attachment, and `attachEnv` at lines 768-788 forces `TERM=xterm-256color`. Initializing that terminal requires the missing database, so the error affects both new and pre-upgrade sessions whenever the nightly's client attaches.

The release smoke at `frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:108-112` runs only `tmux -V`, which does not initialize terminal capabilities and therefore cannot catch this failure.

## Suggested Fix

- Make the bundled ncurses lookup portable, either by compiling the required terminal descriptions as ncurses fallbacks (at minimum `xterm-256color`) or by packaging a minimal terminfo tree and setting an AO-owned `TERMINFO` path for bundled tmux attaches. Do not retain the CI build prefix as the runtime default.
- Add an artifact smoke test that creates an isolated tmux server and performs a real PTY attach with `TERM=xterm-256color`; checking `tmux -V` alone is insufficient.
- Verify both macOS architectures and Linux release artifacts because the same build script produces all three.

## Impact

- TUI-mode agent sessions cannot be reliably attached in the affected nightly.
- Existing sessions regress immediately after update even though their agent processes were started before the update.
- The problem is harness-independent because it occurs in the tmux client before agent output is rendered.

## Related

- PR [#4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293) introduced the bundled tmux artifact and attachment path.
- PR [#2488](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2488) is the earlier open bundled-tmux implementation in the same subsystem.

## Bug

The packaged macOS/Linux app invokes AO's bundled tmux binary, but the runtime is not fully isolated from tmux state owned by the user.

**Source:** User report and follow-up design discussion in an AO task on 2026-08-24/25 (no public chat URL)
**Analyzed against:** `5e408467b`
**Confidence:** High
**Priority:** P1 — a socket collision can direct AO input, restart, or destroy operations at a user-owned tmux session.

## Reproduction

1. Start a user tmux server using the named socket `tmux -L ao`, or keep a same-named session on the default server.
2. Configure `~/.tmux.conf` with options/hooks that are inappropriate for AO.
3. Launch packaged AO and create or restore a TUI session.
4. Observe that AO uses the fixed `-L ao` namespace, allows a newly started server to load user configuration, and probes the default tmux socket when the AO-named server does not contain a matching session.

A custom `TMUX_TMPDIR` also changes where `-L ao` resolves, so the apparently private namespace is still controlled by inherited host environment.

## Root Cause

- `frontend/src/main.ts` injects the constant `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME=ao`.
- `backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go` invokes tmux with `-L ao`, without an explicit `-f` configuration.
- The adapter caches socket discovery in memory and falls back to the machine default socket using only a matching session name as evidence.
- The tmux control process inherits a surrounding `TMUX` identity.
- `backend/internal/tmuxbin/resolve.go` may fall through to a PATH tmux if a recognizable packaged layout is missing its bundled sibling.

## Fix

- Derive a stable absolute socket path from the daemon run-file identity and use `-S` for every tmux operation.
- Keep the socket inode beside the run file; use a bounded, validated `/tmp` directory alias only when macOS's AF_UNIX path ceiling requires it.
- Pass `-f /dev/null` so AO never loads system/user tmux configuration or plugins.
- Remove automatic named/default socket discovery; every control operation stays on the AO-private socket.
- Remove only tmux identity/internal selector variables while preserving the user's workload environment, and refresh that environment for every new or respawned pane.
- Fail closed when a packaged daemon's bundled tmux is missing.
- Keep Windows on the existing ConPTY adapter.

## Impact

- User tmux servers and AO can collide across socket namespaces.
- AO may inherit user hooks/plugins/options and fail unpredictably.
- A stale AO handle plus a same-named user session can cause AO to operate on foreign state.
- Machines without system tmux should continue to work through the bundled artifact; the terminfo regression in that artifact is tracked separately.

## Related

- [Issue #4382](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4382) / [PR #4385](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4385) — bundled tmux terminfo artifact failure.
- [PR #4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293) — introduced bundled tmux and the fixed `-L ao` namespace.
- [Issue #2662](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/2662) / [PR #2664](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2664) — broader cross-data-dir session namespace collision.

## Bug

Importing a local folder that is **already registered** as a project dead-ends the Import project modal: it shows the raw daemon error `A project at this path is already registered (PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED)` with only *"Choose a different folder to try again"* + **Cancel**. There is no path to the already-registered project, even though the daemon tells the client exactly which project it is.

Reporter's ask: instead of this error, offer an option to **go to that project**.

**Source:** Discord `#bug-triage` (2026-08-25)
**Reported by:** @maaz
**Analyzed against:** `origin/main` @ `4c3f4d72e`
**Confidence:** High — full chain traced end-to-end (daemon → envelope → apiClient → CreateProjectFlow)
**Priority:** medium — degraded UX, workaround exists (find the project manually in the sidebar)

## Reproduction

1. Have a project registered at path `P` (it is in the sidebar)
2. `+` → **Import project** → *Choose a project folder* → select `P` in the OS picker
3. Confirm creation in the agent sheet
4. Daemon returns `409 PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED`
5. Modal re-opens in the bare folder-picker state: red error box with the raw message, footer *"Choose a different folder to try again"*, only **Cancel** available — a dead end

![Import project modal showing the PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED dead-end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/i-trytoohard/codex-startup-factory/issue-assets-import-registered-deadend/.issue-assets/import-registered-deadend/modal.png)

## Root Cause

The daemon already returns everything needed to recover — the renderer discards it at every layer.

**The daemon side is fine:**

- `backend/internal/service/project/service.go:196-200` — `Add()` returns `apierr.Conflict("PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED", "A project at this path is already registered", map[string]any{"existingProjectId": existing.ID, "suggestedProjectId": ...})`
- `backend/internal/httpd/envelope/envelope.go:44` — `Details map[string]any json:"details,omitempty"` — so `details.existingProjectId` **is on the wire** in the 409 response.

**Where the renderer drops it:**

1. `frontend/src/renderer/routes/_shell.tsx` (`createProject`, ~L424-432):
   ```ts
   const failure = new Error(apiErrorMessage(error)) as Error & { code?: string };
   failure.code = apiErrorCode(error);
   throw failure;
   ```
   Only `message` + `code` survive. `error.details` — which carries `existingProjectId` — is dropped on the floor. There is no `apiErrorDetails()` helper at all (`frontend/src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts` has `apiErrorMessage` / `apiErrorCode` / `apiErrorRequestId` only).

2. `frontend/src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts` (`apiErrorMessage`) renders `` `${body.message} (${code})` `` — which is exactly the `(PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED)` suffix visible in the screenshot. Raw daemon code leaked into UI copy.

3. `frontend/src/renderer/components/CreateProjectFlow.tsx:212-235` (`createProject` catch): `code` **is** extracted (line 213) but is only branched on for `NOT_A_GIT_REPO` / `PROJECT_UNBORN` repository-setup recovery. There is no branch for `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED` / `ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED`. So: `setError(message)`, and since `shouldScanCreateFailure()` (line 421-426) *explicitly returns `false`* for `(PATH|ID)_ALREADY_REGISTERED`, `validationScan` stays `null` → `CreateProjectFolderDialog` renders the bare dashed picker + error box + footer `createProject.footerChoose` ("Choose a different folder to try again", `en.json:166`).

4. Pre-flight doesn't help either: the folder scan (`frontend/src/main/import-folder-scan.ts`, `scanGitRepo`) only knows git facts (bare, unborn, no remote, reserved name). It has no access to AO's registered-project list, so the user learns about the conflict only **after** confirming.

## Fix

1. **Carry the conflict payload**: in `_shell.tsx` `createProject` (and `cloneProject` for symmetry), attach `error.details` (or minimally `existingProjectId`) to the thrown error, e.g. add an `apiErrorDetails(error)` helper in `api-client.ts` next to the existing ones.
2. **Branch on the code** in `CreateProjectFlow`'s catch: for `PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED`, render a dedicated state in `CreateProjectFolderDialog` — "This folder is already registered as a project" with a primary **Go to project** action (navigate to `existingProjectId` via the existing project navigation; the project is already in the sidebar) and secondary *Choose a different folder*. Same pattern applies to `ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED`.
3. **Optional belt-and-braces**: during the folder scan, flag the selected repo as "already registered" (the renderer already has the workspace/project list) so the user finds out at picker time, before confirming.

## Impact

- Any user who re-imports a folder that's already registered (new machine, restored disk, or simply forgetting it's in the long sidebar list) hits a hard dead-end that reads like a system fault rather than guidance.
- The error copy exposes the raw daemon code (`PATH_ALREADY_REGISTERED`) verbatim, inconsistent with the rest of the import flow's human-readable messaging.

## Related

- #2721 — same flow, non-Git/nested import error messaging (different failure class, same "raw error in modal" shape)

## Bug

Claude Code Plan mode is described as **“Planning mode, no actual tool execution.”** In native ChatUI QA it executed tools and persisted a plan file under `~/.claude/plans`, outside the session worktree, even though the prompt explicitly prohibited tools and file changes.

**Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419)  
**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA  
**Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; relevant paths rechecked on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, source-built `ao` (`dev`), verified daemon on port 3001  
**Priority:** P1 — the UI presents a false safety boundary  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced natively, filesystem side effect captured, and rendering/forwarding path traced

## Reproduction

1. Open a Claude Code session in ChatUI.
2. Select **Plan** in the permission-mode menu.
3. Prompt it to produce a plan while explicitly saying not to execute tools or modify files.
4. Observe Read/Write activity and a new Markdown plan under `~/.claude/plans`.
5. Deny the later “Ready to code?” prompt; the plan file already exists.

- `backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/config_options.go:172` forwards provider descriptions.

- Mode changes are forwarded to ACP; AO does not currently impose a tool/write policy at this boundary.

## Fix direction

Prefer truthful provider-specific disclosure unless AO can enforce a strict read-only mode. Add a provider contract test that observes writes outside the worktree.

## Acceptance

- Plan-mode copy never promises a boundary AO does not enforce.
- Claude-specific behavior explains provider-owned plan artifacts before selection.
- `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-01` passes in strict mode.

## Evidence

![Claude Plan mode writes a plan file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/b7d4a8dc8cf8843be42a3c0bb183e35103ccd06f/docs/qa/chatui-2026-08-25/screenshots/22-plan-mode-writes-plan-file.png)

## Bug

Switching from a busy Chat session to Terminal immediately selects destructive `interrupt`, cancelling the active tool/turn and queued instructions without a Finish-versus-Stop choice. The reverse Terminal-to-Chat direction already presents that policy dialog.

**Source:** [ChatUI QA and regression harness PR #4419](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4419)  
**Reported by:** Dhruv Sharma via local native-Electron QA  
**Analyzed against:** `d71acca1e13ddd9ab3a01a43f029853686f4c693`; exact hard-coded path remains on `04b676c9abd2fac4505081b0c099e079a30bde57`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, source-built AO, verified daemon on port 3001  
**Priority:** P1 — active and queued work can be destroyed without consent  
**Confidence:** High — reproduced natively and exact transition policy traced

## Reproduction

1. Start a Chat turn that runs a long tool, such as `sleep 20`.
2. Optionally queue a follow-up.
3. Click the top-bar action to switch to Terminal UI.
4. Observe no policy dialog; the transition begins immediately.
5. The native TUI shows the tool/turn as interrupted.

## Expected

Idle/no-queue Chat may drain directly. Active or queued Chat must show **Finish work, then switch** (safe default) versus **Stop now and switch**, name affected queue/draft state, and make no interrupt request before explicit consent.

## Actual

The renderer sends `policy: interrupt` immediately and temporarily exposes a mismatched surface while the destructive transition runs.

## Root cause

- `frontend/src/renderer/components/SessionView.tsx:704` hard-codes `interrupt` for Chat-to-Terminal before checking busy/queued state.
- `backend/internal/service/chat/controller.go:1389` applies interrupt semantics, cancelling the durable queue and provider work.

## Fix direction

Reuse the existing policy dialog in both directions. Derive the safe default from active/queued state and prove no transition POST occurs before user choice.

## Acceptance

- Busy Chat always offers drain versus interrupt.
- Default focus is **Finish work, then switch**.
- Drain preserves accepted active/queued work.
- Interrupt occurs only after explicit **Stop now** consent.
- `npm run qa:chatui -- --grep MQA-05` passes in strict mode.

## Bug

Chat-mode sessions launch their structured provider controller with `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` explicitly empty and never persist a `browser_capability_verifier`. As a result, `ao browser` and capability-protected preview-server commands fail for every Chat worker even when the current bundled rewrite binary and Electron browser runtime support them.

**Source:** Independently reproduced in disposable AO-managed Chat session `agent-orchestrator-214` while reassessing the externally hosted process attached to session `agent-orchestrator-211` (211 was not contacted or modified)  
**Reported:** 2026-08-25  
**Analyzed against:** [`dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99) (`origin/main`, exact match to the triage checkout)  
**AO version:** freshly built rewrite CLI reports `dev`; bundled daemon reports `dev` and SHA-256 `3bb56a325b7e10ff35560386e118b2a5d2b7c258724c1f7cc9c586d89e251fb3`  
**Environment:** macOS arm64, Go `1.26.4`, daemon healthy/ready on port `3001`  
**Confidence:** **High** — reproduced with an explicit current rewrite binary and traced through issuance, persistence, provider-env injection, authorization, tests, and introducing history.  
**Priority:** **P2** — browser automation is unavailable to all Chat sessions; switching/creating as TUI is a bounded workaround.

## Scope correction: managed Chat vs externally hosted process

Session `agent-orchestrator-211` does **not** establish this managed-Chat defect. Its durable AO row is `tui`, has nonempty runtime handle/launch IDs, and already stores a 43-character browser verifier. The process reporting the missing environment variable is a separately hosted `node_repl` process carrying AO session/worktree context, not the AO-managed TUI runtime that received the launch credential. A recovered/stale bearer presented from that external process correctly failed with `BROWSER_CAPABILITY_INVALID`.

AO has no repository-owned refresh/delegation endpoint that can safely disclose a new bearer to an already-running arbitrary external process, and possession of `AO_SESSION_ID` alone must not authorize browser control. Whether hosted-process attachment should gain a separate authenticated capability-delegation protocol is outside this issue and requires an explicit security design.

This issue remains valid and is scoped only to **AO-managed structured Chat controllers**, independently proven by session `agent-orchestrator-214`: it was created through `ao spawn --mode chat`, has provider conversation and controller generation IDs, has no terminal runtime IDs, received commands through the durable Chat conversation, and reproduced both an empty verifier and missing environment bearer.

## Reproduction

1. Build the exact current rewrite CLI and verify it is talking to the Go daemon, not a legacy PATH binary:

   ```sh
   git checkout dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99
   (cd backend && go build -o /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro ./cmd/ao)
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro version
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro status --json
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro browser --help
   ```

   Observed: version `dev`; daemon state `ready`, health `ok`, port `3001`; `browser` includes `status`, `open`, `snapshot`, and the other current commands.

2. Spawn a fresh disposable Chat worker using the same absolute binary:

   ```sh
   /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro spawn \
     --project agent-orchestrator \
     --name triage-chat-browser \
     --harness codex \
     --mode chat \
     --prompt 'Report whether AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY is set, then run /tmp/ao-chat-browser-repro browser status.'
   ```

3. The fresh controller reports:

   ```text
   AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY=unset
   ao browser requires the owning session capability (AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY is not set)
   ```

   The absolute rewrite command exits `2`.

4. Inspect only verifier lengths, never credential values:

   ```sql
   SELECT id, session_mode, length(browser_capability_verifier)
   FROM sessions
   WHERE id = '<fresh-chat-session>';
   ```

   Observed for disposable `agent-orchestrator-214`: `chat | 0`. Existing TUI rows launched on the same daemon have verifier length `43`.

The disposable session was terminated after reproduction.

## Expected

Every AO-managed Chat controller should receive a fresh, unguessable, session-scoped browser bearer in its own provider/runtime environment, while only the one-way verifier is durably stored before the worker can present the token. The owning Chat worker should pass `ao browser status`; another session, a stale launch token, an empty token, and a terminated session should remain unauthorized.

## Root cause

The shared environment builder intentionally clears all browser credentials:

- [`runtimeEnv`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3773-L3796) sets `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY`, `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN`, and `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN_STDIN` to empty values.
- [`launchRuntimeEnv`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3799-L3813) is the only layer that calls the browser authority, injects the bearer, and returns its verifier.
- [`persistBrowserCapabilityVerifier`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L3815-L3830) stores the verifier before process launch to close the eager-worker authorization race.

TUI spawn and restore use the secure launch path and persist the verifier:

- [TUI spawn](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L899-L905)
- [TUI restore](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go#L1978-L1985)

Every structured-controller launch bypasses it:

- [fresh Chat spawn](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go#L128-L147) calls `runtimeEnv` and passes the cleared map to `StartChat`;
- [Chat restore/reconcile](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/chat_spawn.go#L290-L329) repeats the same call;
- [direct Chat agent switching](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/session_manager/agent_switching_chat.go#L27-L40) builds the target environment with `runtimeEnv` and later hands that map to the target `StartChat`.

The provider layer faithfully passes `cfg.Env` into both driver start and resume, so the credential is already absent before the Codex/ACP boundary: [chat service dispatch](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/service/chat/service.go#L340-L370).

Authorization then correctly rejects the request because Chat has neither half of the split credential: [browser service authorization](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/blob/dd47a7547f5533a7fb2b109c67eb98c632a47b99/backend/internal/service/browser/service.go#L77-L94).

### History

[PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472) introduced Chat on 2026-08-06 with `runtimeEnv` as its environment seam. [PR #3473](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3473), merged on 2026-08-08 as commit [`c9e1c676b`](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/commit/c9e1c676baee8ab2e860a8110f2539a460e73a11), split browser credentials into an ephemeral bearer plus durable verifier and changed the terminal spawn/restore paths to `launchRuntimeEnv`; it did not update the already separate Chat launch paths. `git blame` still attributes both Chat calls to PR #3472.

## Affected modes and paths

- **Affected:** fresh Chat sessions for every harness whose structured driver receives `ChatStart.Env` (confirmed live with Codex; generic code path also covers ACP Chat drivers).
- **Affected:** Chat controller resume/reconcile after daemon/controller recovery.
- **Affected:** TUI → Chat interface transitions and Chat source rollback paths that relaunch through `resumeChatController`.
- **Affected:** Chat → Chat agent switching and its target/recovery launches.
- **Not affected:** normal TUI spawn/restore, which already issue, persist, and inject the credential.

## Security requirements for the fix

This is an authorization-availability omission, not evidence of an auth bypass. The existing boundary must remain intact:

- mint a fresh random bearer for each controller launch and bind its verifier to the AO session ID;
- persist **only** the one-way verifier before the provider process can run an eager browser command;
- inject the bearer only into the owning Chat provider environment; never store it in SQLite, metadata/DTO JSON, logs, error envelopes, conversation events, or frontend state;
- continue clearing privileged `AO_BROWSER_RUNTIME_TOKEN*` values so the Electron runtime credential cannot leak to a worker;
- rotate on relaunch so stale controller tokens fail, and preserve cross-session rejection;
- sequence rotation correctly during interface/agent switching: do not invalidate a still-live source controller prematurely, and ensure rollback/recovery receives a newly matching token/verifier pair;
- do not weaken browser/preview authorization or introduce a global/shared capability to make Chat pass.

The current domain field is already `json:"-"`, and the authority uses constant-time comparison with a verifier bound to the session ID; those properties should remain unchanged.

## Required tests

1. Fresh Chat spawn issues exactly one pair, persists the verifier before `StartChat`, injects a nonempty bearer into `ChatStart.Env`, retains the verifier through `ControllerReady`, and authorizes only that session.
2. Project/inherited env cannot supply or override `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY` or either privileged browser-runtime secret.
3. Issuer failure or empty credentials aborts Chat spawn before controller start and exercises the existing workspace/session rollback contract.
4. Chat resume/reconcile rotates the pair before provider resume; the new bearer succeeds and the old bearer fails.
5. TUI → Chat transition, Chat → Chat agent switch, source rollback, and restart recovery each end with one matching bearer/verifier pair without invalidating a still-running source during a reversible phase.
6. Cross-session, empty, stale, and terminated-session capabilities remain rejected; no bearer appears in stored session records, API responses, logs, or durable conversation events.
7. End-to-end regression: start the desktop/browser runtime, spawn a fresh Chat worker with an explicit rewrite binary on `:3001`, and verify `ao browser status` succeeds without relying on PATH.

Current tests cover `launchRuntimeEnv` and browser authorization in isolation, and Chat tests assert only that a generic env/session ID reaches the controller. No test asserts issuance or verifier persistence for Chat.

## PATH shadowing is separate

A bare `ao browser status` in the disposable worker also resolved to a legacy binary and returned `unknown command "browser"`. That is **not** the cause established here: the same worker reproduced the missing-capability error with the absolute current rewrite binary. This report therefore does not combine the capability defect with legacy/PATH pinning behavior.

## Recommended implementation scope

Introduce one controller-launch credential preparation boundary shared by fresh Chat launch, Chat resume/reconcile, interface transition, and Chat agent switching. It should return the provider env plus verifier, durably establish the verifier at the correct lifecycle/saga boundary before `StartChat`, preserve/rotate it through controller commits, and explicitly model rollback/recovery ordering. Reuse the existing authority and storage column; no schema/API relaxation should be necessary.

This is not a trivial one-line fix because agent/interface switching has reversible pre-stop phases and post-stop rollback/recovery. No speculative fix PR was opened during triage.

## Verification performed

```text
go build ./...                                                        PASS
go test ./internal/session_manager -run 'Test(RuntimeEnv|ChatSpawnStartsControllerAndNoRuntime|ResumeExitedChatSessionDoesNotRequireTerminalRuntimeHandle)' -count=1  PASS
go test ./internal/service/browser -count=1                          PASS
```

## Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues and PRs for `AO_BROWSER_CAPABILITY`, `browser_capability_verifier`, `owning session capability`, `chat ao browser`, `chat browser automation`, and `session owned browser`. No duplicate report or fix was found.

## Related

- [Issue #3360](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/3360) — Chat/TUI architecture and lifecycle invariants.
- [PR #3472](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3472) — introduced the structured Chat controller paths.
- [PR #3473](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/3473) — introduced session-owned browser automation and the split bearer/verifier security model.

## Problem

#4465 reverted the backend half of the private-hashed-tmux-socket migration (#4393) — `runtimeselect.New()` now calls `tmux.New(tmux.Options{})` with no `SocketPath`, so `socketForSession`'s `r.socketName` is empty by default and legacy sessions are found directly on the machine's default socket.

However, the desktop Electron main process still independently opts every packaged launch back into the private socket:

```
frontend/src/main.ts:845
...(bundledTmuxBinary ? { AO_TMUX_BINARY: bundledTmuxBinary, AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME: "ao" } : {}),
```

`tmux.New` reads `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME` from the environment when `Options.SocketName` is empty (`tmux.go:287-289`), so any packaged desktop build with a staged bundled tmux binary — the common case — still runs with `socketName = "ao"`, and hits the exact symptom #4465 set out to fix.

## Reproduce

On a machine with tmux sessions that predate this whole migration (i.e. living only on the default socket):

```
$ /path/to/bundled/tmux -L ao has-session -t <session-id>
error connecting to /private/tmp/tmux-<uid>/ao (No such file or directory)

$ /path/to/bundled/tmux -L default has-session -t <session-id>
(exit 0 — session is alive)
```

`socketForSession` (`tmux.go`) only crosses the migration boundary to the legacy default socket when the private-socket probe output matches `sessionMissingOutput` ("can't find session"/"session not found") or `serverNotRunningOutput` ("no server running"). Neither matches "error connecting ... No such file or directory" — the exact message tmux gives when the private socket file was never created, which is guaranteed on first launch of a build with this env var reintroduced against pre-existing legacy sessions. The probe returns `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive`, and every legacy session's terminal pane shows "Terminal disconnected — reattaching…" indefinitely, with `reconcile: reap pass failed` / `reaper: probe error reported as failed fact` log spam for every session.

## Why this survived #4465's testing

#4465's revert is real and correct for the backend default, but its own repro/verification path (`env -u AO_TMUX_BINARY ... npm run lint` etc., per the PR body) unsets `AO_TMUX_BINARY`, which also disables the `bundledTmuxBinary` branch in `main.ts` that sets `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME`. So the revert's own verification never exercises the actual packaged-desktop code path where the symptom reappears.

## Fix options

- Drop the `AO_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME: "ao"` half of `main.ts:845` (keep `AO_TMUX_BINARY` only) so the packaged desktop app matches the reverted backend default, or
- If the private socket is still wanted opportunistically from the desktop launcher, extend `socketForSession`'s migration-boundary check to also treat "error connecting ... no such file or directory" as definitive (this is what a private socket that was simply never created looks like — distinct from a running server going transiently unreachable, which the existing `transientServerFailureOutput`/#3475 guard is right to keep ambiguous).

## Verification after fix

On a machine with pre-existing default-socket sessions, launch the packaged desktop app and confirm the terminal pane attaches immediately instead of showing "Terminal disconnected — reattaching…", and `daemon.log` has no `reconcile reap ...: probe: ... liveness probe inconclusive: error connecting` entries for those sessions.

## Related
- #4465 (this issue's cause — the backend-only revert)
- #4393 (original migration)

## Bug

Dragging across text already typed into the Chat composer creates a real DOM selection, but the highlight is effectively invisible. Users cannot tell which part of a draft is selected before replacing, cutting, or copying it.

**Source:** AO chat report on 2026-08-26 | **Analyzed against:** `c4abb8afc4a305fbd20c6d3955a2c7808d78e7d4` | **AO version:** `dev` (desktop `0.10.3`)
**OS reproduced on:** macOS 26.5, arm64 | **Daemon:** ready on `127.0.0.1:3001`
**Priority:** P2 — draft editing is significantly degraded; keyboard-only selection is possible but still has no visual confirmation.
**Confidence:** High — the exact pointer path is automated, the DOM range remains non-collapsed, and the rendered selection/surface contrast is measured.

## Reproduction

1. Open a Chat-mode session with an existing conversation.
2. Type a multi-word draft in the composer.
3. Drag the pointer across part or all of the draft.
4. Observe that no visible highlight appears, even though `window.getSelection()` contains a non-collapsed range.

The focused Playwright reproduction types a wrapped draft, drag-selects it through actual pointer events, verifies the DOM selection, then measures the composited selection-highlight contrast. On current `main` it fails:

```text
Expected: >= 1.5
Received:    1.013160847557346
```

## Root cause

`frontend/src/renderer/components/chat/ComposerEditor.tsx` styles selected text with:

```text
selection:bg-accent/30
```

In Tailwind's theme bridge, `accent` is the subtle surface token (`--accent`), not the stronger product accent. In the light theme it is `oklch(0.967 0.001 286.375)` over the composer's `oklch(0.985 0 0)` card surface. At 30% alpha the composited contrast is only `1.013:1`, so the browser paints a valid selection that looks unselected.

This was introduced with the Lexical composer in [PR #4331](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4331), commit `b8e3d57f25`.

## Fix

Use a theme-aware foreground/primary selection tint with enough alpha to remain visibly distinct from the composer surface, and keep an E2E regression that proves both:

- pointer drag creates a durable selection of the typed draft;
- the composited highlight/surface contrast is at least `1.5:1`.

## Evidence

Before — the draft is selected in the DOM, but no highlight is perceptible:

![Before: invisible chat composer selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-composer-selection-visibility/.issue-assets/chat-composer-selection-visibility/before.png)

After — the same automated pointer selection is visibly highlighted:

![After: visible chat composer selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issue-assets-chat-composer-selection-visibility/.issue-assets/chat-composer-selection-visibility/after.png)

## Impact

- Users cannot safely replace or cut a portion of a drafted instruction.
- Copy/cut may operate on text with no visible confirmation of the range.
- The failure looks like pointer selection is broken even though the browser selection model is working.

## Related

- [#4268](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/issues/4268) — read-only surfaces inherit `user-select: none`; adjacent symptom, different mechanism. The composer already computes `user-select: text`.
- [PR #4443](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4443) — restores selection on read-only content surfaces; it does not change the composer's selection highlight.

input.body:
## Feature Description

On Windows, standalone shell terminals always launch whichever shell the daemon finds first in a **hardcoded probe order** — `pwsh.exe` → `powershell.exe` → `ComSpec` → `cmd.exe`. There is no way for the user to choose a different default shell, and **Git Bash is never considered at all**.

Requested: a user-facing option (app setting and/or per-terminal picker) to select the default shell for standalone terminals, with Git Bash as a first-class choice alongside PowerShell / cmd.

## Current behavior (code anchors)

- `backend/internal/service/shellterm/loginshell.go` — `resolveUserLoginShell()` → `resolveWindowsShell()`: hardcoded candidate list `["pwsh.exe", "powershell.exe"]` then `ComSpec`/`cmd.exe` fallback. No user preference is consulted, no Git Bash probe (e.g. `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`), no override hook.
- `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go` — `OpenShellTerminalInput` has no shell/shellPath field, so `POST /api/v1/shell-terminals` cannot express a shell choice per open request either.
- `frontend/src/main.ts` (`runLoginShell`, ~line 635) — login-shell env detection runs a shell too; a changed default should be honored consistently there.
- Unix already prefers `$SHELL` (`loginshell.go:24`), which is why this reads as Windows-only — but note the Unix sibling bug with non-POSIX shells: #3788 (fish).

## Motivation

- Reported by a Windows user who lives in Git Bash: **SahilG** in the `#feature-requests` Discord thread *"default terminal option"* — currently the **most upvoted feature request** there.
- Git Bash is a daily-driver shell for many Windows developers; getting PowerShell instead makes the standalone terminal pane a pane they immediately `exit` out of.
- PowerShell-first probe order also surprises cmd users the same way (SahilG perceived "only cmd is supported" — either way, the user loses).

## Proposed Solution

1. **Setting:** add a `shell` preference (e.g. `"auto" | "git-bash" | "pwsh" | "powershell" | "cmd" | custom path`) to app settings, surfaced in the desktop app's Settings UI.
2. **Resolution order:** `resolveUserLoginShell()` should consult the preference first; `"auto"` keeps today's behavior. Git Bash detection: `where git` → `<Git>\bin\bash.exe` (or `bash.exe` on PATH), launched with `--login -i`.
3. **Wire API:** optionally extend `OpenShellTerminalInput` with an optional per-request `shell` override so the UI can offer a per-terminal picker (⊞ new-terminal dropdown) without extra round-trips.
4. **Validation:** reject-with-message or fall back to `auto` when the configured shell path doesn't exist at open time (consistent with the "must not open something unusable" rule in `loginshell.go:17-19`).
5. **Regenerate API artifacts** (`npm run api`) if DTOs change.

## Alternatives Considered

- Environment-variable-only override (e.g. `AO_SHELL`) — cheap but undiscoverable; fine as a power-user extra, not a substitute for a setting.
- Doing nothing / documenting PowerShell-first — rejected: most-upvoted request, and the fix is well-bounded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Windows user can set Git Bash as the default shell; new standalone terminals launch in Git Bash (`--login -i`)
- [ ] PowerShell (pwsh + Windows PowerShell) and cmd remain selectable; `"auto"` preserves current behavior
- [ ] Custom shell path supported, with clear error/fallback when it's missing
- [ ] Preference honored by the login-shell env detection path (`runLoginShell`), not just terminal spawn
- [ ] Unix behavior unchanged (`$SHELL` still wins)
- [ ] OpenAPI spec + `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` regenerated if request DTOs change

## Environment

- OS: Windows (feature is Windows-facing; Unix already honors `$SHELL`)
- Surface: standalone shell terminals (`/terminals` screen) — shellterm service → daemon → ConPTY

_Filed from Discord thread "default terminal option" (#feature-requests). Reporter: @SahilG; picked up by @Vaibhaav-Tiwari._
input.title: feat(windows,shell-terminals): selectable default shell for standalone terminals (Git Bash, PowerShell, cmd)
